tmp2 <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = DE %>% select(SubjectId, cervical_dilation_cesarean_section, DEMODECD, DEOPEDELCD, DEOXYYNCD, DEOXY, DEOXYH, DEEPIYNCD, DEPUDYNCD, DEEPYNCD, DECOMPYNCD, DECOMP1CD, DECOMP2CD, DECOMP3CD, DECOMP4CD, DECOMP5CD, DECOMP6CD, DECOMP7CD, DECOMP8CD, DECOMP9CD, DECOMP99CD, DEPPH, DEASIYNCD, DEASIGRACD, DEURCYNCD, DEURC1CD, DEURC2CD, DEURC3CD, DEURCDISCD), by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp1 = if_else(
      condition = is.na(cervical_dilation_cesarean_section) & (DEMODECD == 1 | (DEMODECD == 2 & DEOPEDELCD != 3 & DEOPEDELCD != 5)), 
      true = 1, 
      false = if_else(
        condition = is.na(cervical_dilation_cesarean_section) & DEMODECD == 2 & (DEOPEDELCD == 3 | DEOPEDELCD == 5), 
        true = 2, 
        false = NA, 
        missing = NA
      ), 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    tmp2 = if_else(
      condition = is.na(DEOXY) & DEOXYYNCD == 0, 
      true = 1, 
      false = if_else(
        condition = is.na(DEOXY) & DEOXYYNCD == 1, 
        true = 2, 
        false = NA, 
        missing = NA
      ), 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    tmp3 = if_else(
      condition = is.na(DEOXYH) & DEOXYYNCD == 0, 
      true = 1, 
      false = if_else(
        condition = is.na(DEOXYH) & DEOXYYNCD == 1, 
        true = 2, 
        false = NA, 
        missing = NA
      ), 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    tmp4 = if_else(
      condition = is.na(DEASIGRACD) & DEASIYNCD == 0, 
      true = 3, 
      false = DEASIGRACD, 
      missing = DEASIGRACD
    )
  )
tmp3 <- tmp2 %>% 
  bind_rows(tmp2 %>% mutate(Treatment_allocated_str = "Overall"))
table_labor_delivery_characteristics3 <- create_table_summary_statistics(table = tmp1, data = tmp3, group = "Treatment_allocated_str")

# Creating a table in HTML

tmp2 <- 0
tmp3 <- (1:dim(table_labor_delivery_characteristics)[1])[which(substr(x = table_labor_delivery_characteristics$Characteristic, start = 1, stop = 1) != "-")]
knitr::kable(x = table_labor_delivery_characteristics, format = "html", align = c("l", rep(x = "c", times = tmp1 - 1)), caption = paste("Table 9: Labor and delivery characteristics in the full-analysis set (", dim(FA_set)[1], " subjects), overall and by treatment group. Abbreviations: HELLP -- hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets; IQR -- interquartile range; SD -- standard deviation.", sep = "")) %>% kable_classic(full_width = TRUE, html_font = "Computer Modern") %>% row_spec(row = tmp2, bold = TRUE) %>% row_spec(row = tmp3, italic = TRUE)
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

*Table 14* displays summary statistics of endpoints of subjects in the FA set (*n* = `r dim(FA_set)[1]`), overall and by treatment group. Continuous variables are presented with mean, standard deviation, median, and interquartile range. Categorical variables are presented with absolute and relative frequencies (i.e., numbers and percentages).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Writing a Stata DTA file with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
# NOTE: The time variable is set to missing if the time variable equals 0, i.e., if the onset of active labor and delivery occur at the same time or delivery first. Is this correct?
tmp1 <- DE %>% 
  select(SubjectId, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event) %>% 
  mutate(
    time = if_else(condition = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery <= 0, true = NA, false = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, missing = NA), 
    event = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event
  ) %>% 
  select(SubjectId, time, event)
tmp2 <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId")
write_dta(data = tmp2, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery.dta"))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery.dta", clear

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event (event of interest or competing event)
tabulate event, missing

* Generating a string variable for the type of event (event of interest or competing event)
label define event 1 "Spontaneous vaginal birth" 2 "Operative delivery", replace
label values event event
decode event, generate(event_str)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Generating numeric variables for the cumulative incidence functions and the higher and lower bounds of their confidence interval
* NOTE: This takes the competing event into account.
* NOTE: The 1st command calculates the cumulative incidences overall.
* NOTE: The 2nd command calculates the cumulative incidences per allocated treatment group.
stcompet ci_overall = ci hi_overall = hi lo_overall = lo, compet1(2) level(95)
stcompet ci_group = ci hi_group = hi lo_group = lo, compet1(2) by(Treatment_allocated_str) level(95)

* Generating numeric variables for the cumulative incidence function and the higher and lower bounds of its confidence interval for the event of interest
quietly generate ci1_overall = ci_overall if event == 1
quietly generate hi1_overall = hi_overall if event == 1
quietly generate lo1_overall = lo_overall if event == 1
quietly generate ci1_group = ci_group if event == 1
quietly generate hi1_group = hi_group if event == 1
quietly generate lo1_group = lo_group if event == 1

* Generating numeric variables for the cumulative incidence function and the higher and lower bounds of its confidence interval for the competing event
quietly generate ci2_overall = ci_overall if event == 2
quietly generate hi2_overall = hi_overall if event == 2
quietly generate lo2_overall = lo_overall if event == 2
quietly generate ci2_group = ci_group if event == 2
quietly generate hi2_group = hi_group if event == 2
quietly generate lo2_group = lo_group if event == 2

* Plotting the cumulative incidence functions and their confidence intervals (version 1)
quietly graph twoway ///
  (line ci1_group _t, sort(_t) lcolor(stc1)) ///
  (line ci2_group _t, sort(_t) lcolor(stc2)) ///
  (rarea lo1_group hi1_group _t, vertical sort color(stc1%25)) ///
  (rarea lo2_group hi2_group _t, vertical sort color(stc2%25)), ///
  ytitle("Crude cumulative incidence") xtitle("Time since the onset of active labor (min)") ///
  subtitle(, size(*0.75)) ///
  legend(order(1 2) label(1 "Spontaneous vaginal birth") label(2 "Operative delivery") rows(1) title("Treatment arm")) ///
  by(Treatment_allocated_str, legend(position(6)) title("Crude cumulative incidence functions") note("Graphs by allocated treatment arm")) ///
  name(tmp1, replace) ///
  saving("Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 1.gph", asis replace)
quietly graph export "Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 1.tif", name(tmp1) as(tif) replace width(10000)

* Plotting the cumulative incidence functions and their confidence intervals (version 2A)
quietly graph twoway ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", sort(_t) lcolor(stc1)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", sort(_t) lcolor(stc2)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", sort(_t) lcolor(stc3)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", sort(_t) lcolor(stc4)), ///
  ytitle("Crude cumulative incidence") xtitle("Time since the onset of active labor (min)") ///
  legend(order(1 2 3 4) label(1 "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide") label(2 "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo") label(3 "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide") label(4 "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo") rows(2) size(*0.75) title("Treatment arm")) ///
  by(event_str, rows(1) legend(position(6)) title("Crude cumulative incidence functions") note("Graphs by mode of delivery")) ///
  name(tmp2, replace) ///
  saving("Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 2A.gph", asis replace)
quietly graph export "Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 2A.tif", name(tmp2) as(tif) replace width(10000)

* Plotting the cumulative incidence functions and their confidence intervals (version 2B)
quietly graph twoway ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", sort(_t) lcolor(stc1)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", sort(_t) lcolor(stc2)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", sort(_t) lcolor(stc3)) ///
  (line ci_group _t if Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", sort(_t) lcolor(stc4)), ///
  ytitle("Crude cumulative incidence") xtitle("Time since the onset of active labor (min)") ///
  legend(order(1 2 3 4) label(1 "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide") label(2 "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo") label(3 "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide") label(4 "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo") rows(2) size(*0.75) title("Treatment arm")) ///
  by(event_str, cols(1) legend(position(6)) title("Crude cumulative incidence functions") note("Graphs by mode of delivery")) ///

  saving("Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 2B.gph", asis replace)

  "- Yes",                                                               "spontaneous_vaginal_delivery",                                 "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- Missing",                                                           "spontaneous_vaginal_delivery",                                 "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = ""), 
  "Vaginal delivery",                                                    "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- No",                                                                "vaginal_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- Yes",                                                               "vaginal_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- Missing",                                                           "vaginal_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = ""), 
  "Mode of delivery",                                                    "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- Spontaneous vaginal delivery",                                      "mode_of_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- Instrumental delivery",                                             "mode_of_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "2"), 
  "- Cesarean delivery",                                                 "mode_of_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "3"), 
  "- Missing",                                                           "mode_of_delivery",                                             "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = ""), 
  "OASIS",                                                               "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- No",                                                                "tmp1",                                                         "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- Yes",                                                               "tmp1",                                                         "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- Not applicable",                                                    "tmp1",                                                         "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "2"), 
  "- Missing",                                                           "tmp1",                                                         "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = ""), 
  "Time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery", "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- Type of event",                                                     "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- - Censoring",                                                       "time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event",               "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- - Event of interest",                                               "time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event",               "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- - Competing event",                                                 "time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event",               "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "2"), 
  "- - Missing",                                                         "time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event",               "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = ""), 
  "- Survival time",                                                     "",                                                             "calculate_no_summary_statistics",             list(), 
  "- - Median survival time for the event of interest",                  list("time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event", "tmp2"), "calculate_summary_statistics_time_to_event1", list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- - Not applicable",                                                  "tmp3",                                                         "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- - Missing",                                                         "time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery",                     "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2",   list(digits = 1, level = "")
)
tmp2 <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = DE %>% select(SubjectId, spontaneous_vaginal_delivery, vaginal_delivery, mode_of_delivery, DEASIYNCD, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery), by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  mutate(

      condition = vaginal_delivery == 1,

    ),

      false = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    tmp3 = if_else(
      condition = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery <= 0, 
      true = 1, 
      false = NA, 
      missing = NA
    )
  )
tmp3 <- tmp2 %>% 
  bind_rows(tmp2 %>% mutate(Treatment_allocated_str = "Overall"))

### Key Secondary Endpoints

We plot the crude cumulative incidences of spontaneous vaginal delivery and operative delivery as functions of time since the onset of active labor.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Creating a plot of the cumulative incidence functions and their confidence intervals (version 1)
tmp <- read_dta(file = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Survival-Time Data.dta")) %>% 
  filter(event_str != "") %>% 
  select(Treatment_allocated_str, event_str, ci_group, hi_group, lo_group, `_t`) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_allocated_str = factor(
      x = Treatment_allocated_str, 
      levels = c("Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
      labels = c("Bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide", "Bicarbonate", "Hyoscine butylbromide", "Double placebo (ref.)")
    ), 
    event_str = factor(
      x = event_str, 
      levels = c("Spontaneous vaginal birth", "Operative delivery"), 
      labels = c("Spontaneous vaginal birth", "Operative delivery")
    ), 
    `_t` = `_t` / 60
  ) %>% 
  arrange(`_t`)
plot_time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_cumulative_incidence1 <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = `_t`, group = event_str)) + 
  geom_ribbon(mapping = aes(ymin = lo_group, ymax = hi_group, fill = event_str), alpha = 0.25) + 
  geom_line(mapping = aes(y = ci_group, color = event_str)) + 
  facet_wrap(
    facets = vars(Treatment_allocated_str), 
    nrow = 2, 
    scales = "fixed", 
    dir = "h"
  ) + 
  labs(
    x = "Time since the onset of active labour (h)", 
    y = "Crude cumulative incidence", 
    title = NULL
  ) + 
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      title = "Mode of delivery", 
      direction = "vertical", 
      nrow = 1, 
      byrow = TRUE
    ), 
    fill = guide_legend(
      title = "Mode of delivery", 
      direction = "vertical", 
      nrow = 1, 
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  ) + 
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12), 
    legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
plot_time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_cumulative_incidence1
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Saving the plot as a PDF file
ggsave(
  filename = "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 1.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "pdf", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)

# Saving the plot as a PNG file
ggsave(
  filename = "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Delivery - Crude Cumulative Incidence - Version 1.png", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "png", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Primary Endpoint

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, spontaneous_vaginal_delivery, spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_best_case, spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Peroral_bicarbonate = if_else(
      condition = Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide" | Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", 
      true = 1, 
      false = 0, 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide = if_else(
      condition = Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide" | Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", 
      true = 1, 
      false = 0, 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Peroral_bicarbonate = if_else(
      condition = Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide" | Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", 
      true = 1, 
      false = 0, 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide = if_else(
      condition = Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide" | Treatment_allocated_str == "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", 
      true = 1, 
      false = 0, 
      missing = NA
    ), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI,

  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"),

    ),

We consider the primary endpoint, which is spontaneous vaginal delivery.

### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 3* displays the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 3: Log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery looks fairly linear, and the analyses of spontaneous vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 4* displays the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 4: Log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of spontaneous vaginal delivery also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of spontaneous vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in spontaneous vaginal delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being spontaneous vaginal delivery. The Bonferroni-corrected significance level is set at 0.01663.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1 <- glm(
  formula = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)

tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])

tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Sensitivity Analyses

#### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in spontaneous vaginal delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the PP set
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6 <- glm(
  formula = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_PP_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results) <- tmp4
colnames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model6_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Subgroup Analyses

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated oral treatment (dichotomous variable), allocated intravenous treatment (dichotomous variable), the interaction between allocated oral treatment and allocated intravenous treatment (dichotomous variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in spontaneous vaginal delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7 <- glm(
  formula = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_best_case ~ Peroral_bicarbonate * Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7), confint(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7, level = 0.95)))
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
# NOTE: The "linearHypothesis" function in the "car" package may also be used to calculate p-values, e.g., car::linearHypothesis(model = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7, hypothesis.matrix = c("Peroral_bicarbonate + Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide = 0")).
tmp1 <- coef(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7)
tmp2 <- vcov(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7)
tmp3 <- list()
tmp3[[1]] <- tmp1["Peroral_bicarbonate"] + tmp1["Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"]
tmp3[[2]] <- tmp1["Peroral_bicarbonate"]
tmp3[[3]] <- tmp1["Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"] + tmp1["Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"]
tmp3[[4]] <- tmp1["Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"]
tmp4 <- list()
tmp4[[1]] <- sqrt(x = tmp2["Peroral_bicarbonate", "Peroral_bicarbonate"] + tmp2["Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide", "Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"] + 2 * tmp2["Peroral_bicarbonate", "Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"])
tmp4[[2]] <- sqrt(x = tmp2["Peroral_bicarbonate", "Peroral_bicarbonate"])
tmp4[[3]] <- sqrt(x = tmp2["Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide", "Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"] + tmp2["Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide", "Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"] + 2 * tmp2["Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide", "Peroral_bicarbonate:Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"])
tmp4[[4]] <- sqrt(x = tmp2["Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide", "Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide"])
tmp5 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp3)) {
  tmp5[[i]] <- exp(x = tmp3[[i]])
}
tmp6 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp4)) {
  tmp6[[i]] <- exp(x = tmp3[[i]] - qnorm(p = 0.975, mean = 0, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE) * tmp4[[i]])
}
tmp7 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp4)) {
  tmp7[[i]] <- exp(x = tmp3[[i]] + qnorm(p = 0.975, mean = 0, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE) * tmp4[[i]])
}
tmp8 <- list()
tmp8[[1]] <- 2 * pnorm(q = abs(x = tmp3[[1]] / tmp4[[1]]), lower.tail = FALSE)
tmp8[[2]] <- summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7)$coefficients[2, "Pr(>|z|)"]
tmp8[[3]] <- 2 * pnorm(q = abs(x = tmp3[[3]] / tmp4[[3]]), lower.tail = FALSE)
tmp8[[4]] <- summary(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7)$coefficients[3, "Pr(>|z|)"]
tmp9 <- c("Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide: Peroral bicarbonate", "Intravenous placebo: Peroral bicarbonate", "Peroral bicarbonate: Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral placebo: Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide")
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp9)) {
  spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[i]] <- cbind(tmp5[[i]], tmp6[[i]], tmp7[[i]], tmp8[[i]])
  rownames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[i]]) <- tmp9[i]
  colnames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[i]]) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
}
# spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual
rbind(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[1]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[2]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[3]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_manual[[4]])
rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- emmeans::emmeans(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7, specs = ~ Peroral_bicarbonate | Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide, type = "link")
tmp2 <- emmeans::emmeans(object = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7, specs = ~ Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide | Peroral_bicarbonate, type = "link")
tmp3 <- emmeans::contrast(object = tmp1, method = "revpairwise", adjust = "none")
tmp4 <- emmeans::contrast(object = tmp2, method = "revpairwise", adjust = "none")
tmp5 <- summary(object = tmp3, type = "response", infer = TRUE, level = 0.95)
tmp6 <- summary(object = tmp4, type = "response", infer = TRUE, level = 0.95)
tmp7 <- list()
tmp7[[1]] <- tmp5$odds.ratio[2]
tmp7[[2]] <- tmp5$odds.ratio[1]
tmp7[[3]] <- tmp6$odds.ratio[2]
tmp7[[4]] <- tmp6$odds.ratio[1]
tmp8 <- list()
tmp8[[1]] <- tmp5$asymp.LCL[2]
tmp8[[2]] <- tmp5$asymp.LCL[1]
tmp8[[3]] <- tmp6$asymp.LCL[2]
tmp8[[4]] <- tmp6$asymp.LCL[1]
tmp9 <- list()
tmp9[[1]] <- tmp5$asymp.UCL[2]
tmp9[[2]] <- tmp5$asymp.UCL[1]
tmp9[[3]] <- tmp6$asymp.UCL[2]
tmp9[[4]] <- tmp6$asymp.UCL[1]
tmp10 <- list()
tmp10[[1]] <- tmp5$p.value[2]
tmp10[[2]] <- tmp5$p.value[1]
tmp10[[3]] <- tmp6$p.value[2]
tmp10[[4]] <- tmp6$p.value[1]
tmp11 <- c("Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide: Peroral bicarbonate", "Intravenous placebo: Peroral bicarbonate", "Peroral bicarbonate: Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral placebo: Intravenous hyoscine butylbromide")
spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp11)) {
  spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[i]] <- cbind(tmp7[[i]], tmp8[[i]], tmp9[[i]], tmp10[[i]])
  rownames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[i]]) <- tmp11[i]
  colnames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[i]]) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
}
# spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results
rbind(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[1]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[2]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[3]], spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results[[4]])
rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7,

tmp3[[4]] <- tmp2$estimate[which(x = tmp2$Peroral_bicarbonate == 0)] * 100

tmp4[[2]] <- tmp1$conf.low[which(x = tmp1$Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide == 0)] * 100
tmp4[[3]] <- tmp2$conf.low[which(x = tmp2$Peroral_bicarbonate == 1)] * 100
tmp4[[4]] <- tmp2$conf.low[which(x = tmp2$Peroral_bicarbonate == 0)] * 100
tmp5 <- list()
tmp5[[1]] <- tmp1$conf.high[which(x = tmp1$Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide == 1)] * 100
tmp5[[2]] <- tmp1$conf.high[which(x = tmp1$Intravenous_hyoscine_butylbromide == 0)] * 100
tmp5[[3]] <- tmp2$conf.high[which(x = tmp2$Peroral_bicarbonate == 1)] * 100

spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_margins <- list()
for (i in 1:length(tmp7)) {

  colnames(spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_margins[[i]]) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
}
# spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model7_results_margins

rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

### Post-Hoc Analyses

We perform some post-hoc analyses where we stratify the main analysis of the primary endpoint by study site.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
for (i in c("01", "02", "03", "04", "05", "06", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11")) {
  tmp <- glm(
    formula = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    data = spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_FA_set, 
    subset = SiteCode == i, 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
  assign(x = paste("spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model8", i, sep = "_"), value = tmp)
}
rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
for (i in c("01", "02", "03", "04", "05", "06", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11")) {
  tmp1 <- get(x = paste("spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model8", i, sep = "_"))
  tmp2 <- summary(tmp1)$coefficients[2:4,]
  tmp3 <- rownames(tmp2)
  tmp4 <- exp(x = confint(object = tmp1, parm = tmp3, level = 0.95))
  tmp5 <- substr(x = tmp3, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp3, type = "chars"))
  tmp6 <- exp(x = tmp2[, "Estimate"])
  tmp7 <- tmp4[, 1]
  tmp8 <- tmp4[, 2]
  tmp9 <- tmp2[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  tmp10 <- cbind(tmp6, tmp7, tmp8, tmp9)
  rownames(tmp10) <- tmp5
  colnames(tmp10) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
  assign(x = paste("spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model8", i, "results", sep = "_"), value = tmp10)
}
rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
for (i in c("01", "02", "03", "04", "05", "06", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11")) {
  tmp1 <- get(x = paste("spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model8", i, sep = "_"))
  tmp2 <- avg_comparisons(
    model = tmp1, 
    variables = "Treatment_", 
    type = "response", 
    conf_level = 0.95, 
    comparison = "difference"
  )
  tmp3 <- tmp2$contrast
  tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp3, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp3, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
  tmp5 <- tmp2$estimate * 100
  tmp6 <- tmp2$conf.low * 100
  tmp7 <- tmp2$conf.high * 100
  tmp8 <- tmp2$p.value
  tmp9 <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
  rownames(tmp9) <- tmp4
  colnames(tmp9) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
  assign(x = paste("spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model8", i, "results", "margins", sep = "_"), value = tmp9)
}
rm(i, list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

## Secondary Endpoints

We now consider the secondary endpoints.

### Vaginal Delivery

```{r, include = FALSE}

tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)

  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>%

  )
vaginal_delivery_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>%

vaginal_delivery_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>%

  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>%

  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName,

```

We consider vaginal delivery.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of vaginal delivery and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 5* displays the log odds of vaginal delivery as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 5: Log odds of vaginal delivery as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of vaginal delivery against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- vaginal_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(vaginal_delivery, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_vaginal_delivery_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of vaginal delivery vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_vaginal_delivery_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Vaginal Delivery as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of vaginal delivery looks fairly linear, and the analyses of vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of vaginal delivery and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 6* displays the log odds of vaginal delivery as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 6: Log odds of vaginal delivery as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of vaginal delivery against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- vaginal_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(vaginal_delivery, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_vaginal_delivery_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of vaginal delivery vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_vaginal_delivery_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Vaginal Delivery as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of vaginal delivery also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in vaginal delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for vaginal delivery based on the FA set
vaginal_delivery_model1 <- glm(
  formula = vaginal_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = vaginal_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(vaginal_delivery_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(vaginal_delivery_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = vaginal_delivery_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
vaginal_delivery_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(vaginal_delivery_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(vaginal_delivery_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
vaginal_delivery_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = vaginal_delivery_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

Missingness in vaginal delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}

)

```

tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

  model = vaginal_delivery_model2,

)

##### Worst-Case (Single) Imputation

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in vaginal delivery is handled using worst-case (single) imputation, with the worst-case scenario being cesarean delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for vaginal delivery based on the FA set
vaginal_delivery_model3 <- glm(
  formula = vaginal_delivery_worst_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = vaginal_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(vaginal_delivery_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(vaginal_delivery_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = vaginal_delivery_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
vaginal_delivery_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(vaginal_delivery_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(vaginal_delivery_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
vaginal_delivery_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

  model = vaginal_delivery_model3, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
vaginal_delivery_model3_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(vaginal_delivery_model3_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(vaginal_delivery_model3_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
vaginal_delivery_model3_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Mode of Delivery

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, mode_of_delivery, mode_of_delivery_best_case, mode_of_delivery_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
mode_of_delivery_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
mode_of_delivery_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
mode_of_delivery_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider mode of delivery.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effects of age on the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 7* and *Figure 8* display the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, respectively, as functions of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 7: Log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- mode_of_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5), 
    tmp2 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 1, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA), 
    tmp3 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 2, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp4 = mean(tmp2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = mean(tmp3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp6 = log(x = tmp5 / tmp4, base = exp(1)), 
    tmp7 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp8 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp9 = mean(x = c(tmp7, tmp8), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_age1 <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp9, y = tmp6)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_age1
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Instrumental Delivery Versus Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 8: Log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- mode_of_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5), 
    tmp2 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 1, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA), 
    tmp3 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 3, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp4 = mean(tmp2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = mean(tmp3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp6 = log(x = tmp5 / tmp4, base = exp(1)), 
    tmp7 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp8 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp9 = mean(x = c(tmp7, tmp8), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_age2 <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp9, y = tmp6)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_age2
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Cesarean Delivery Versus Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effects of age on the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, respectively, look fairly linear, and the analyses of mode of delivery will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effects of BMI on the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 9* and *Figure 10* display the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, respectively, as functions of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 9: Log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- mode_of_delivery_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5), 
    tmp2 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 1, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA), 
    tmp3 = if_else(condition = mode_of_delivery == 2, true = 1, false = 0, missing = NA)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp4 = mean(tmp2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = mean(tmp3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp6 = log(x = tmp5 / tmp4, base = exp(1)), 
    tmp7 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp8 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp9 = mean(x = c(tmp7, tmp8), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_BMI1 <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp9, y = tmp6)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_mode_of_delivery_BMI1
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Instrumental Delivery Versus Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effects of BMI on the log odds of instrumental delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery and the log odds of cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery, respectively, also look fairly linear, and the analyses of mode of delivery will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in mode of delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery based on the FA set
mode_of_delivery_model1 <- multinom(
  formula = mode_of_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  data = mode_of_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(mode_of_delivery_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the relative risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals and p values based on the fitted regression model
# NOTE: See https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/63222/getting-p-values-for-multinom-in-r-nnet-package regarding calculation of p values.
tmp1 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model1)$coefficients[, 2:4]
tmp2 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model1)$standard.errors[, 2:4]
tmp3 <- colnames(tmp1)
tmp4 <- exp(x = confint(object = mode_of_delivery_model1, parm = tmp3, level = 0.95))
tmp5 <- substr(x = tmp3, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp3, type = "chars"))
tmp6 <- t(x = exp(x = tmp1))
tmp7 <- tmp4[, 1, ]
tmp8 <- tmp4[, 2, ]
tmp9 <- t(x = pnorm(q = -abs(x = tmp1 / tmp2), mean = 0, sd = 1) * 2)
mode_of_delivery_model1_results1 <- cbind(tmp6[, "2"], tmp7[, "2"], tmp8[, "2"], tmp9[, "2"])
mode_of_delivery_model1_results2 <- cbind(tmp6[, "3"], tmp7[, "3"], tmp8[, "3"], tmp9[, "3"])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results1) <- tmp5
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results2) <- tmp5
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results1) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results2) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model1_results1
mode_of_delivery_model1_results2
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = mode_of_delivery_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "probs", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
mode_of_delivery_model1_results1_margins <- cbind(tmp4[1:3], tmp5[1:3], tmp6[1:3], tmp7[1:3])
mode_of_delivery_model1_results2_margins <- cbind(tmp4[4:6], tmp5[4:6], tmp6[4:6], tmp7[4:6])
mode_of_delivery_model1_results3_margins <- cbind(tmp4[7:9], tmp5[7:9], tmp6[7:9], tmp7[7:9])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results1_margins) <- tmp3[1:3]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results2_margins) <- tmp3[4:6]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results3_margins) <- tmp3[7:9]
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results1_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results2_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model1_results3_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model1_results1_margins
mode_of_delivery_model1_results2_margins
mode_of_delivery_model1_results3_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

##### Worst-Case (Single) Imputation

We fit an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in mode of delivery is handled using worst-case (single) imputation, with the worst-case scenario being cesarean delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery based on the FA set
mode_of_delivery_model3 <- multinom(
  formula = mode_of_delivery_worst_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  data = mode_of_delivery_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(mode_of_delivery_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the relative risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals and p values based on the fitted regression model
# NOTE: See https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/63222/getting-p-values-for-multinom-in-r-nnet-package regarding calculation of p values.
tmp1 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model3)$coefficients[, 2:4]
tmp2 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model3)$standard.errors[, 2:4]
tmp3 <- colnames(tmp1)
tmp4 <- exp(x = confint(object = mode_of_delivery_model3, parm = tmp3, level = 0.95))
tmp5 <- substr(x = tmp3, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp3, type = "chars"))
tmp6 <- t(x = exp(x = tmp1))
tmp7 <- tmp4[, 1, ]
tmp8 <- tmp4[, 2, ]
tmp9 <- t(x = pnorm(q = -abs(x = tmp1 / tmp2), mean = 0, sd = 1) * 2)
mode_of_delivery_model3_results1 <- cbind(tmp6[, "2"], tmp7[, "2"], tmp8[, "2"], tmp9[, "2"])
mode_of_delivery_model3_results2 <- cbind(tmp6[, "3"], tmp7[, "3"], tmp8[, "3"], tmp9[, "3"])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results1) <- tmp5
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results2) <- tmp5
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results1) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results2) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model3_results1
mode_of_delivery_model3_results2
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = mode_of_delivery_model3, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "probs", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
mode_of_delivery_model3_results1_margins <- cbind(tmp4[1:3], tmp5[1:3], tmp6[1:3], tmp7[1:3])
mode_of_delivery_model3_results2_margins <- cbind(tmp4[4:6], tmp5[4:6], tmp6[4:6], tmp7[4:6])
mode_of_delivery_model3_results3_margins <- cbind(tmp4[7:9], tmp5[7:9], tmp6[7:9], tmp7[7:9])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results1_margins) <- tmp3[1:3]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results2_margins) <- tmp3[4:6]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results3_margins) <- tmp3[7:9]
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results1_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results2_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model3_results3_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model3_results1_margins
mode_of_delivery_model3_results2_margins
mode_of_delivery_model3_results3_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in mode of delivery is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(mode_of_delivery_model4_results3_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(mode_of_delivery_model4_results3_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(mode_of_delivery_model4_results3_margins[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Comments` = rep(x = "Spontaneous vaginal delivery as the base category", times = 4)
  )

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in mode of delivery is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted multinomial logistic regression model for mode of delivery based on the PP set
mode_of_delivery_model5 <- multinom(
  formula = mode_of_delivery_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  data = mode_of_delivery_PP_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(mode_of_delivery_model5)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the relative risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals and p values based on the fitted regression model
# NOTE: See https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/63222/getting-p-values-for-multinom-in-r-nnet-package regarding calculation of p values.
tmp1 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model5)$coefficients[, 2:4]
tmp2 <- summary(mode_of_delivery_model5)$standard.errors[, 2:4]
tmp3 <- colnames(tmp1)
tmp4 <- exp(x = confint(object = mode_of_delivery_model5, parm = tmp3, level = 0.95))
tmp5 <- substr(x = tmp3, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp3, type = "chars"))
tmp6 <- t(x = exp(x = tmp1))
tmp7 <- tmp4[, 1, ]
tmp8 <- tmp4[, 2, ]
tmp9 <- t(x = pnorm(q = -abs(x = tmp1 / tmp2), mean = 0, sd = 1) * 2)
mode_of_delivery_model5_results1 <- cbind(tmp6[, "2"], tmp7[, "2"], tmp8[, "2"], tmp9[, "2"])
mode_of_delivery_model5_results2 <- cbind(tmp6[, "3"], tmp7[, "3"], tmp8[, "3"], tmp9[, "3"])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results1) <- tmp5
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results2) <- tmp5
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results1) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results2) <- c("Relative risk ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model5_results1
mode_of_delivery_model5_results2
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = mode_of_delivery_model5, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "probs", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
mode_of_delivery_model5_results1_margins <- cbind(tmp4[1:3], tmp5[1:3], tmp6[1:3], tmp7[1:3])
mode_of_delivery_model5_results2_margins <- cbind(tmp4[4:6], tmp5[4:6], tmp6[4:6], tmp7[4:6])
mode_of_delivery_model5_results3_margins <- cbind(tmp4[7:9], tmp5[7:9], tmp6[7:9], tmp7[7:9])
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results1_margins) <- tmp3[1:3]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results2_margins) <- tmp3[4:6]
rownames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results3_margins) <- tmp3[7:9]
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results1_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results2_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
colnames(mode_of_delivery_model5_results3_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
mode_of_delivery_model5_results1_margins
mode_of_delivery_model5_results2_margins
mode_of_delivery_model5_results3_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```
