### Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
# NOTE: We restrict the data frames to vaginal deliveries.
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, vaginal_delivery, DEASIYNCD, DEASIYNCD_best_case, DEASIYNCD_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
DEASIYNCD_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  filter(vaginal_delivery == 1) %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-vaginal_delivery)
DEASIYNCD_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  filter(vaginal_delivery == 1) %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-vaginal_delivery)
DEASIYNCD_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  filter(vaginal_delivery == 1) %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-vaginal_delivery)
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider obstetric anal sphincter injury, restricted to vaginal deliveries.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 11* displays the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 11: Log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury as a function of age. Abbreviations: OASIS -- obstetric anal sphincter injury."}
# Plotting the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEASIYNCD_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEASIYNCD, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEASIYNCD_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of OASIS vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEASIYNCD_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury looks fairly linear, and the analyses of obstetric anal sphincter injury will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 12* displays the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 12: Log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index; OASIS -- obstetric anal sphincter injury."}
# Plotting the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEASIYNCD_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEASIYNCD, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEASIYNCD_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of OASIS delivery vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEASIYNCD_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of obstetric anal sphincter injury also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of obstetric anal sphincter injury will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for obstetric anal sphincter injury, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set, restricted to vaginal deliveries. Missingness in obstetric anal sphincter injury is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no obstetric anal sphincter injury.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for obstetric anal sphincter injury based on the FA set
DEASIYNCD_model1 <- glm(
  formula = DEASIYNCD_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = DEASIYNCD_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(DEASIYNCD_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(DEASIYNCD_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = DEASIYNCD_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
DEASIYNCD_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(DEASIYNCD_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(DEASIYNCD_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEASIYNCD_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = DEASIYNCD_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
DEASIYNCD_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(DEASIYNCD_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(DEASIYNCD_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEASIYNCD_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

We fit a crude binary logistic regression model for obstetric anal sphincter injury, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set, restricted to vaginal deliveries. Missingness in obstetric anal sphincter injury is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no obstetric anal sphincter injury.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting a crude logistic regression model for obstetric anal sphincter injury based on the FA set
DEASIYNCD_model2 <- glm(
  formula = DEASIYNCD_best_case ~ Treatment_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = DEASIYNCD_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(DEASIYNCD_model2)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(DEASIYNCD_model2)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = DEASIYNCD_model2, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
DEASIYNCD_model2_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(DEASIYNCD_model2_results) <- tmp4
colnames(DEASIYNCD_model2_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEASIYNCD_model2_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = DEASIYNCD_model2, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
DEASIYNCD_model2_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(DEASIYNCD_model2_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(DEASIYNCD_model2_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEASIYNCD_model2_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Creating a tibble for the results from the statistical analysis of the secondary endpoints
results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Obstetric anal sphincter injury", times = 4),

    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Sensitivity analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "Vaginal deliveries", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Binary logistic regression", times = 4),

    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Best-case (single) imputation", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = nobs(object = DEASIYNCD_model2), times = 4),

    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4),

### Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
# NOTE: The time variable is set to missing if the time variable equals 0, i.e., if the onset of active labor and delivery occur at the same time or delivery first. Is this correct?
tmp1 <- DE %>% 
  select(SubjectId, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_PP_set, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event_event_of_interest) %>% 
  mutate(
    time = if_else(condition = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery <= 0, true = NA, false = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, missing = NA), 
    .after = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    event = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event, 
    .after = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event
  ) %>% 
  rename(
    time_mean_imputation_ITT_set = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    time_mean_imputation_FA_set = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    time_mean_imputation_PP_set = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_mean_imputation_PP_set, 
    event_event_of_interest = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event_event_of_interest
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery, time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_event))
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    time_mean_imputation = time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_mean_imputation_PP_set))
time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    time_mean_imputation = time_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_mean_imputation_PP_set))
time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    time_mean_imputation = time_mean_imputation_PP_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_mean_imputation_PP_set))
write_dta(data = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_ITT_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - ITT Set.dta"))
write_dta(data = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_FA_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta"))
write_dta(data = time_from_onset_active_labor_to_delivery_PP_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - PP Set.dta"))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumptions of linear effects of age and BMI on the natural logarithm of the subdistribution hazard function. Then, we check the assumption of proportional subdistribution hazards (PSH).

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Creating variables for age squared and age cubed
quietly generate Age_squared = Age^2
quietly generate Age_cubed = Age^3

* Creating variables for BMI squared and BMI cubed
quietly generate BMI_squared = BMI^2
quietly generate BMI_cubed = BMI^3

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, inlcuding quadratic and cubic terms of age and BMI
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age Age_squared Age_cubed BMI BMI_squared BMI_cubed i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
testparm Age_squared Age_cubed
testparm BMI_squared BMI_cubed
testparm Age_squared Age_cubed BMI_squared BMI_cubed

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, including interaction terms between treatment and analysis time
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) tvc(i.Treatment_) texp(_t) level(95) allbaselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
test [tvc]

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, including interaction terms between treatment and the natural logarithm of analysis time
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) tvc(i.Treatment_) texp(ln(_t)) level(95) allbaselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
test [tvc]
```

There is not solid evidence of non-linearity, and the analyses of time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for age and BMI as continuous variables. Furthermore, there is no solid evidence against the PSH assumption. Hence, we will use Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression to analyze time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Setting the working directory of the current R session
setwd(wd)

# Setting the working directory for "knitr" during knitting
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = wd)
```

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method
frame create results2

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the delta method
frame results2: quietly svmat B, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames B
local tmp2 = 0
frame results2: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results2: order var, first

* Saving the Stata datasets
local tmp = c(pwd)
frame results1: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 1.dta", replace
frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 1 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

* Dropping the frames containing the results of the regression analysis and of the delta method
frame drop results1 results2
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

```

# Calculating the subdistribution hazard ratio with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1 <- read_dta(file = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 1.dta"))
tmp1 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$b[2:4]
tmp2 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$ll[2:4]
tmp3 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$ul[2:4]
tmp4 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$pvalue[2:4]
tmp5 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$var[2:4]

time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in subdistribution hazards using the delta method.

time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp1, tmp2, tmp3, tmp4)
rownames(time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- tmp5
colnames(time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- c("Difference in subdistribution hazards", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

We fit a crude adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model2_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model2_results_margins[, "P value"], NA),

  )

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method
frame create results2

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the delta method
frame results2: quietly svmat B, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames B
local tmp2 = 0
frame results2: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results2: order var, first

* Saving the Stata datasets
local tmp = c(pwd)
frame results1: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 3.dta", replace
frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 3 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

* Dropping the frames containing the results of the regression analysis and of the delta method
frame drop results1 results2
```

```

tmp2 <- time_from_onset_active_labor_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model3$ll[2:4]

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the onset of active labor to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery

use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - PP Set.dta", clear

drop time event

tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the PP set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method

}
quietly label list Treatment_

local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}

* Saving the Stata datasets

frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 4 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

#### Post-Hoc Analyses

We perform some post-hoc analyses using the restricted mean survival time as a summary measure.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the Onset of Active Labor to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Defining a local macro for the maximum value of the variable for time to delivery for all spontaneous vaginal deliveries
summarize time if event == 1
local time_svd_max = r(max)

* Creating a new time variable of which the value for all operative deliveries is imputed with the maximum value for all spontaneous vaginal deliveries plus 1
quietly generate time2 = .
quietly replace time2 = time               if event == 1
quietly replace time2 = `time_svd_max' + 1 if event == 2

* Tabulating the variable for the allocated treatment
tabulate Treatment_, missing
tabulate Treatment_, missing nolabel

* Listing contents of value labels for the variable for the allocated treatment
label list Treatment_

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time2, failure(event == 1)

* Comparing restricted mean survival time
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(360) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(720) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(1080) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(`time_svd_max') level(95) reference(1)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time2, failure(event == 1 2)

* Comparing restricted mean survival time
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(360) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(720) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(1080) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(`time_svd_max') level(95) reference(1)
```

There are some indications of a reduction in time from the onset of active labor to spontaneous vaginal delivery in the arm combining oral placebo and intravenous hyoscine butylbromide compared to the double placebo arm.

### Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
# NOTE: The time variable is set to missing if the time variable equals 0, i.e., if the 1st IMP administration and delivery occur at the same time or delivery first. Is this correct?
tmp1 <- DE %>% 
  select(SubjectId, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_mean_imputation_PP_set, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event_event_of_interest) %>% 
  mutate(
    time = if_else(condition = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery <= 0, true = NA, false = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery, missing = NA), 
    .after = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    event = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event, 
    .after = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event
  ) %>% 
  rename(
    time_mean_imputation_ITT_set = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    time_mean_imputation_FA_set = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_mean_imputation_FA_set,

    event_event_of_interest = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event_event_of_interest
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery, time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_event))
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>%

  ) %>% 
  mutate(

    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_mean_imputation_PP_set))
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(

    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(time_mean_imputation_ITT_set, time_mean_imputation_FA_set, time_mean_imputation_PP_set))
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName,

  ) %>% 
  mutate(

write_dta(data = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_ITT_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - ITT Set.dta"))
write_dta(data = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_FA_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta"))
write_dta(data = time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_delivery_PP_set, path = file.path(getwd(), "Data Files", "Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - PP Set.dta"))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

We consider time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumptions of linear effects of age and BMI on the natural logarithm of the subdistribution hazard function. Then, we check the assumption of proportional subdistribution hazards (PSH).

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Creating variables for age squared and age cubed
quietly generate Age_squared = Age^2
quietly generate Age_cubed = Age^3

* Creating variables for BMI squared and BMI cubed
quietly generate BMI_squared = BMI^2
quietly generate BMI_cubed = BMI^3

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, inlcuding quadratic and cubic terms of age and BMI
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age Age_squared Age_cubed BMI BMI_squared BMI_cubed i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
testparm Age_squared Age_cubed
testparm BMI_squared BMI_cubed
testparm Age_squared Age_cubed BMI_squared BMI_cubed

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, including interaction terms between treatment and analysis time
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) tvc(i.Treatment_) texp(_t) level(95) allbaselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
test [tvc]

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set, including interaction terms between treatment and the natural logarithm of analysis time
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) tvc(i.Treatment_) texp(ln(_t)) level(95) allbaselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Testing linear hypotheses after estimation
test [tvc]
```

There is not solid evidence of non-linearity, and the analyses of time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery will therefore be adjusted for age and BMI as continuous variables. Furthermore, there is no solid evidence against the PSH assumption. Hence, we will use Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression to analyze time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Setting the working directory of the current R session
setwd(wd)

# Setting the working directory for "knitr" during knitting
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = wd)
```

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method
frame create results2

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the delta method
frame results2: quietly svmat B, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames B
local tmp2 = 0
frame results2: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results2: order var, first

* Saving the Stata datasets
local tmp = c(pwd)
frame results1: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 1.dta", replace
frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 1 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

* Dropping the frames containing the results of the regression analysis and of the delta method
frame drop results1 results2
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the subdistribution hazard ratio with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model

tmp1 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$b[2:4]
tmp2 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$ll[2:4]
tmp3 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$ul[2:4]
tmp4 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$pvalue[2:4]
tmp5 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1$var[2:4]
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results <- cbind(tmp1, tmp2, tmp3, tmp4)
rownames(time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results) <- tmp5

time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in subdistribution hazards using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

tmp4 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_margins$pvalue[2:4]
tmp5 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_margins$var[2:4]
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp1, tmp2, tmp3, tmp4)
rownames(time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- tmp5
colnames(time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins) <- c("Difference in subdistribution hazards", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

We fit a crude adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the FA set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method
frame create results2

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the delta method
frame results2: quietly svmat B, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames B
local tmp2 = 0
frame results2: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results2: order var, first

* Saving the Stata datasets
local tmp = c(pwd)
frame results1: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 3.dta", replace
frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 3 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

* Dropping the frames containing the results of the regression analysis and of the delta method
frame drop results1 results2
```

```

tmp2 <- time_from_1st_IMP_administration_to_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery_model3$ll[2:4]

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in the type of event for time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using event-of-interest (single) imputation, i.e., imputing missing values with the event of interest. Missingness in time from the 1st IMP administration to delivery is handled using mean (single) imputation.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery

use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - PP Set.dta", clear

drop time event

rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Creating a numeric variable for the site
encode Site_, generate(Site_num_)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time, failure(event == 1)

* Fitting an adjusted Fine-Gray (competing-risks) regression model for time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery based on the PP set
stcrreg i.Treatment_ Age BMI i.Main_indication_for_induction_ i.Site_num_, compete(event == 2) level(95) baselevels cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the regression analysis
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define A = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the regression analysis
frame create results1

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the regression analysis
frame results1: quietly svmat A, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the number of observations
frame results1: generate n = e(N) in 1

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames A
local tmp2 = 0
frame results1: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results1: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results1: order var, first

* Applying the delta method to estimate the marginal treatment effects
* NOTE: This gives the average differences in the subdistribution hazard rates compared to the reference category, holding the other covariates constant.
margins, dydx(i.Treatment_) level(95) cformat(%9.2f) pformat(%5.3f) sformat(%8.2f)

* Creating a matrix from the results of the delta method
* NOTE: The matrix contains the coefficients with their standard errors, test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals.
matrix define B = r(table)'

* Creating a new frame for the results of the delta method
frame create results2

* Creating variables from the matrix containing the results of the delta method
frame results2: quietly svmat B, names(col)

* Creating a variable for the levels of the variables included in the regression model
local tmp1: rownames B
local tmp2 = 0
frame results2: quietly generate var = ""
foreach lname of local tmp1 {
  local tmp2 = `tmp2' + 1
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`lname'" in `tmp2'
}
quietly label list Treatment_
local tmp3 = r(min)
local tmp4 = r(max)
forvalues i = `tmp3'/`tmp4' {
  local tmp5: label Treatment_ `i'
  frame results2: quietly replace var = "`tmp5'" if strpos(var, "Treatment_") > 0 & substr(var, 1, 1) == "`i'"
}
frame results2: order var, first

* Saving the Stata datasets
local tmp = c(pwd)
frame results1: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 4.dta", replace
frame results2: quietly save "`tmp'\Output Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - Model 4 - Marginal Effects.dta", replace

* Dropping the frames containing the results of the regression analysis and of the delta method
frame drop results1 results2

#### Post-Hoc Analyses

We perform some post-hoc analyses using the restricted mean survival time as a summary measure.

```{stata, include = TRUE}
* Loading the Stata dataset with data related to the time-to-event endpoint corresponding to time from the 1st IMP administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery
local tmp = c(pwd)
use "`tmp'\Data Files\Time From the 1st IMP Administration to Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery - FA Set.dta", clear

* Dropping variables
drop time event

* Renaming variables
rename (time_mean_imputation event_event_of_interest) (time event)

* Tabulating the variable for the type of event
tabulate event, missing

* Defining a local macro for the maximum value of the variable for time to delivery for all spontaneous vaginal deliveries
summarize time if event == 1
local time_svd_max = r(max)

* Creating a new time variable of which the value for all operative deliveries is imputed with the maximum value for all spontaneous vaginal deliveries plus 1
quietly generate time2 = .
quietly replace time2 = time               if event == 1
quietly replace time2 = `time_svd_max' + 1 if event == 2

* Tabulating the variable for the allocated treatment
tabulate Treatment_, missing
tabulate Treatment_, missing nolabel

* Listing contents of value labels for the variable for the allocated treatment
label list Treatment_

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time2, failure(event == 1)

* Comparing restricted mean survival time
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(360) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(720) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(1080) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(`time_svd_max') level(95) reference(1)

* Declearing the data to be survival-time data
stset time2, failure(event == 1 2)

* Comparing restricted mean survival time
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(360) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(720) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(1080) level(95) reference(1)
strmst2 Treatment_, tau(`time_svd_max') level(95) reference(1)
```

There are some indications of a reduction in time from the 1st administration to spontaneous vaginal delivery in the arm combining oral placebo and intravenous hyoscine butylbromide compared to the double placebo arm.
