We consider change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration. *Figure 23* displays change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of age based on the FA set.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 23: Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of age."}
# Plotting change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration against age based on the FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
plot_VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_age <- ggplot(data = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, mapping = aes(x = Age, y = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Change in maternal heart rate (BPM)", title = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Change in Maternal Heart Rate 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

The effect of age on change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration looks fairly linear, albeit with quite a bit of potential outliers, and the analyses of change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration. *Figure 24* displays change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of BMI based on the FA set.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 24: Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration against BMI based on the FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
plot_VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_BMI <- ggplot(data = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, mapping = aes(x = BMI, y = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Change in maternal heart rate (BPM)", title = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Change in Maternal Heart Rate 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

The effect of BMI on change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration also looks fairly linear, albeit with quite a bit of potential outliers, and the analyses of change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

We fit an adjusted linear regression model and do some assumption checks.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the FA set
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0 <- lm(
  formula = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_ + VSPULSE_IMP1, 
  data = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0)
```

We check the normality assumption by inspecting the residuals from the fitted adjusted linear regression model. *Figure 25* and *Figure 26* display a histogram and a normal Q-Q plot, respectively, of the residuals.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 25: Histogram of residuals from an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a histogram of the residuals
hist(
  x = residuals(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Histogram of residuals", 
  sub = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Residuals"
)
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Histogram of Residuals for Change in Maternal Heart Rate 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 26: Normal Q-Q plot of residuals from an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a normal Q-Q plot of the residuals
qqnorm(
  y = residuals(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals", 
  sub = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Theoretical quantiles", 
  ylab = "Sample quantiles"
)
qqline(y = residuals(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0), col = "red")
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals for Change in Maternal Heart Rate 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

Based on a visual assessment of the two plots above, the residuals seem to follow an approximately normal distribution. We therefore conclude that the normality assumption of the fitted linear regression model is fulfilled.

We also check the homoscedasticity assumption by creating a residuals-versus-fitted-versus plot, as shown in *Figure 27*.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 27: Residuals-versus-fitted plot based on an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a residuals-versus-fitted plot
plot(
  x = fitted(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  y = residuals(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Residuals vs. fitted values", 
  sub = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Fitted values", 
  ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Residuals-Versus-Fitted Plot for Change in Maternal Heart Rate 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

Based on a visual assessment of the plot above, the variance of the residuals seems to be fairly constant across all levels of the fitted values. We therefore conclude that the homoscedasticity assumption of the fitted linear regression model is more or less fulfilled.

As the normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of the fitted linear regression model were fulfilled, we use linear regression in the analysis of change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), site (11-level categorical variable), and maternal heart rate at the 1st IMP administration (continuous variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled implicitly by subtracting maternal heart rate at the 1st IMP administration with imputed values from maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the multiple imputed FA set
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1 <- with(
  data = VSPULSE_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = lm(
    formula = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_ + VSPULSE_IMP1, 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled <- pool(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1)
summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp4 <- tmp1$`2.5 %`
tmp5 <- tmp1$`97.5 %`
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in means using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

We fit a crude linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled implicitly by subtracting maternal heart rate at the 1st IMP administration with imputed values from maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting a crude linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the multiple imputed FA set
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2 <- with(
  data = VSPULSE_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = lm(
    formula = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_, 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_pooled <- pool(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2)
summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp4 <- tmp1$`2.5 %`
tmp5 <- tmp1$`97.5 %`
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results) <- tmp2
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in means using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results_margins) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model2_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", times = 4),

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), site (11-level categorical variable), and maternal heart rate at the 1st IMP administration (continuous variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in maternal heart rate 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the FA set
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3 <- lm(
  formula = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_ + VSPULSE_IMP1, 
  data = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- confint(object = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95)
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- tmp1[, "Estimate"]
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in means using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results_margins) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSPULSE_change_IMP1_30_model3_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

    VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_PP_set = VSVAS_mean_imputation_PP_set
  )

  select(SubjectId, VSVAS, VSVAS_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_mean_imputation_PP_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_PP_set) %>%

  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>%

  left_join(y = tmp5, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor,

  ) %>% 
  select(-c(VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_PP_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_PP_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_PP_set))

    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_IMP1_mean_imputation_PP_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_PP_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_ITT_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_FA_set, VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_mean_imputation_PP_set))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
# NOTE: This is based on the multiple imputation of pain score.
VSVAS_multiple_imputation_ITT_set <- as.mids(long = VSVAS_multiple_imputation_ITT_set_complete)
VSVAS_multiple_imputation_FA_set <- as.mids(long = VSVAS_multiple_imputation_FA_set_complete)
VSVAS_multiple_imputation_PP_set <- as.mids(long = VSVAS_multiple_imputation_PP_set_complete)
```

We consider change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration. *Figure 28* displays change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of age based on the FA set.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 28: Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of age."}
# Plotting change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration against age based on the FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
plot_VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_age <- ggplot(data = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, mapping = aes(x = Age, y = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Change in pain score", title = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Change in Pain Score 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

The effect of age on change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration looks fairly linear, albeit with quite a bit of potential outliers, and the analyses of change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration. *Figure 29* displays change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of BMI based on the FA set.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 29: Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration against BMI based on the FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
plot_VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_BMI <- ggplot(data = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, mapping = aes(x = BMI, y = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Change in pain score", title = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Change in Pain Score 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

The effect of BMI on change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration also looks fairly linear, albeit with quite a bit of potential outliers, and the analyses of change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

We fit an adjusted linear regression model and do some assumption checks.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the FA set
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0 <- lm(
  formula = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30 ~ VSVAS_IMP1 + Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  data = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0)
```

We check the normality assumption by inspecting the residuals from the fitted adjusted linear regression model. *Figure 30* and *Figure 31* display a histogram and a normal Q-Q plot, respectively, of the residuals.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 30: Histogram of residuals from an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a histogram of the residuals
hist(
  x = residuals(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Histogram of residuals", 
  sub = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Residuals"
)
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Histogram of Residuals for Change in Pain Score 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 31: Normal Q-Q plot of residuals from an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a normal Q-Q plot of the residuals
qqnorm(
  y = residuals(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals", 
  sub = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Theoretical quantiles", 
  ylab = "Sample quantiles"
)
qqline(y = residuals(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0), col = "red")
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals for Change in Pain Score 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

Based on a visual assessment of the two plots above, the residuals seem to follow an approximately normal distribution. We therefore conclude that the normality assumption of the fitted linear regression model is fulfilled.

We also check the homoscedasticity assumption by creating a residuals-versus-fitted-versus plot, as shown in *Figure 32*.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 32: Residuals-versus-fitted plot based on an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration."}
# Creating a residuals-versus-fitted plot
plot(
  x = fitted(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  y = residuals(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model0), 
  main = "Residuals vs. fitted values", 
  sub = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", 
  xlab = "Fitted values", 
  ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Residuals-Versus-Fitted Plot for Change in Pain Score 30 minutes After the 1st IMP Administration.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
```

Based on a visual assessment of the plot above, the variance of the residuals seems to be fairly constant across all levels of the fitted values. We therefore conclude that the homoscedasticity assumption of the fitted linear regression model is more or less fulfilled.

As the normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of the fitted linear regression model were fulfilled, we use linear regression in the analysis of change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), site (11-level categorical variable), and pain score at the 1st IMP administration (continuous variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled implicitly by subtracting pain score at the 1st IMP administration with imputed values from pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the multiple imputed FA set
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1 <- with(
  data = VSVAS_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = lm(
    formula = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_ + VSVAS_IMP1, 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled <- pool(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1)
summary(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp4 <- tmp1$`2.5 %`
tmp5 <- tmp1$`97.5 %`
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in means using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Creating a tibble for the results from the statistical analysis of the secondary endpoints
results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Continuous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Main analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "None", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Linear regression", times = 4), 
    `Adjustment` = rep(x = "Age (continuous), BMI (continuous), main indication for induction (categorical), site (categorical), and pain score at the 1st IMP administration (continuous)", times = 4), 
    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Multiple imputation of pain score at and 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration before subtraction", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = mean(x = sapply(X = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1$analyses, FUN = nobs)), times = 4), 
    `Allocated treatment` = c(rownames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results), "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Difference in means", times = 4), 
    `Point estiamte` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results[, "Difference in means"], 1), 
    `Lower 95% confidence limit` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Upper 95% confidence limit` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `P value` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Marginal effect measure` = rep(x = "Difference in means", times = 4), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins[, "Difference in means"], 0), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model1_results_margins[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Comments` = rep(x = "", times = 4)
  )
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), site (11-level categorical variable), and pain score at the 1st IMP administration (continuous variable) with fixed effects. Missingness in change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}

colnames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model3_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")

rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), site (11-level categorical variable), and pain score at the 1st IMP administration (continuous variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration is handled implicitly by subtracting pain score at the 1st IMP administration with imputed values from pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted linear regression model for change in pain score 30 minutes after the 1st IMP administration based on the multiple imputed PP set
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4 <- with(
  data = VSVAS_multiple_imputation_PP_set, 
  expr = lm(
    formula = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_ + VSVAS_IMP1, 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_pooled <- pool(object = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4)
summary(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp4 <- tmp1$`2.5 %`
tmp5 <- tmp1$`97.5 %`
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results) <- tmp2
colnames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal differences in means using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal differences in means with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results_margins) <- c("Difference in means", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
VSVAS_change_IMP1_30_model4_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

### Postpartum Hemorrhage > 500 mL

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, DEPPH_dich1, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_PP_set)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
DEPPH_dich1_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich1_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich1_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_PP_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation_PP_set))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 33* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 33: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich1_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich1_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 500 mL as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 34* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 34: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich1_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich1_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 500 mL as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL is handled implicitly by dichotomizing blood loss with imputed values after using mean (single) imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL based on the FA set
DEPPH_dich1_model1 <- glm(
  formula = DEPPH_dich1_mean_imputation ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = DEPPH_dich1_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(DEPPH_dich1_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(DEPPH_dich1_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = DEPPH_dich1_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
DEPPH_dich1_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEPPH_dich1_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = DEPPH_dich1_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Dichotomous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Main analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "None", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Binary logistic regression", times = 4), 
    `Adjustment` = rep(x = "Age (continuous), BMI (continuous), main indication for induction (categorical), and site (categorical)", times = 4), 
    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Mean (single) imputation of blood loss before dichotomization", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = nobs(object = DEPPH_dich1_model1), times = 4), 
    `Allocated treatment` = c(rownames(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results), "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4), 
    `Point estiamte` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results[, "Odds ratio"], 1), 
    `Lower 95% confidence limit` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Upper 95% confidence limit` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `P value` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Marginal effect measure` = rep(x = "Risk difference", times = 4), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins[, "Risk difference"], 0), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(DEPPH_dich1_model1_results_margins[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Comments` = rep(x = "", times = 4)
  )

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 500 mL based on the FA set
DEPPH_dich1_model3 <- glm(
  formula = DEPPH_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = DEPPH_dich1_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(DEPPH_dich1_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(DEPPH_dich1_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = DEPPH_dich1_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
DEPPH_dich1_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(DEPPH_dich1_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(DEPPH_dich1_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEPPH_dich1_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = DEPPH_dich1_model3, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
DEPPH_dich1_model3_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(DEPPH_dich1_model3_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(DEPPH_dich1_model3_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEPPH_dich1_model3_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Postpartum Hemorrhage > 1000 mL

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, DEPPH_dich2, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
DEPPH_dich2_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich2_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich2_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 35* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 35: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich2_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich2_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 1000 mL as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 36* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 36: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich2_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich2_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 1000 mL as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Sensitivity Analyses

We do some sensitivity analyses.

##### Crude Analysis

We fit a crude binary logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL is handled implicitly by dichotomizing blood loss with imputed values after using mean (single) imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting a crude logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 1000 mL based on the FA set
DEPPH_dich2_model2 <- glm(
  formula = DEPPH_dich2_mean_imputation ~ Treatment_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),

### Postpartum Hemorrhage > 1500 mL

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, DEPPH_dich3, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_PP_set)

tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
DEPPH_dich3_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich3_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation = DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_ITT_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_FA_set, DEPPH_dich3_mean_imputation_PP_set))
DEPPH_dich3_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor,

We consider postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 37* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 37: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich3_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich3_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich3_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 1500 mL as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 38* displays the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 38: Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- DEPPH_dich3_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(DEPPH_dich3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich3_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_DEPPH_dich3_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Postpartum Hemorrhage Greater Than 1500 mL as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in postpartum hemorrhage > 1500 mL is handled implicitly by dichotomizing blood loss with imputed values after using mean (single) imputation.

tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = DEPPH_dich3_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
DEPPH_dich3_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(DEPPH_dich3_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(DEPPH_dich3_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
DEPPH_dich3_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)

tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100

tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value

DEPPH_dich3_model1_results_margins

```
