### Urinary Retention in the Delivery Ward

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, urinary_retention_delivery_ward, urinary_retention_delivery_ward_best_case, urinary_retention_delivery_ward_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider urinary retention in the delivery ward.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 39* displays the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 39: Log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_delivery_ward_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_delivery_ward, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_delivery_ward_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_delivery_ward_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention in the Delivery Ward as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention in the delivery ward will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 40* displays the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 40: Log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_delivery_ward_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_delivery_ward, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_delivery_ward_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_delivery_ward_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention in the Delivery Ward as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention in the delivery ward also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention in the delivery ward will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for urinary retention in the delivery ward, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in urinary retention in the delivery ward is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no urinary retention in the delivery ward.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for urinary retention in the delivery ward based on the FA set
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1 <- glm(
  formula = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Creating a tibble for the results from the statistical analysis of the secondary endpoints
results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Urinary retention in the delivery ward", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Dichotomous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Main analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "None", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Binary logistic regression", times = 4), 
    `Adjustment` = rep(x = "Age (continuous), BMI (continuous), main indication for induction (categorical), and site (categorical)", times = 4), 
    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Best-case (single) imputation", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = nobs(object = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1), times = 4), 
    `Allocated treatment` = c(rownames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results), "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4), 
    `Point estiamte` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results[, "Odds ratio"], 1), 
    `Lower 95% confidence limit` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Upper 95% confidence limit` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `P value` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Marginal effect measure` = rep(x = "Risk difference", times = 4), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins[, "Risk difference"], 0), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model1_results_margins[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Comments` = rep(x = "", times = 4)
  )
```

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for urinary retention in the delivery ward, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in urinary retention in the delivery ward is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no urinary retention in the delivery ward.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for urinary retention in the delivery ward based on the PP set
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5 <- glm(
  formula = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_PP_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results) <- tmp4
colnames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_delivery_ward_model5_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Urinary Retention in the Postnatal Ward

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, urinary_retention_postnatal_ward, urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_best_case, urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider urinary retention in the postnatal ward.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 41* displays the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 41: Log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention in the Postnatal Ward as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention in the postnatal ward will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 42* displays the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 42: Log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention in the Postnatal Ward as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention in the postnatal ward also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention in the postnatal ward will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

##### Worst-Case (Single) Imputation

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for urinary retention in the postnatal ward, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in urinary retention in the postnatal ward is handled using worst-case (single) imputation, with the worst-case scenario being urinary retention in the postnatal ward.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for urinary retention in the postnatal ward based on the FA set
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3 <- glm(
  formula = urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_worst_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

)

colnames(urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
urinary_retention_postnatal_ward_model3_results_margins

### Urinary Retention at Hospital Discharge

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- DE %>% select(SubjectId, urinary_retention_hospital_discharge, urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_best_case, urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider urinary retention at hospital discharge.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 43* displays the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 43: Log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_hospital_discharge, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention at Hospital Discharge as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention at hospital discharge will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 44* displays the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 44: Log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(urinary_retention_hospital_discharge, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Urinary Retention at Hospital Discharge as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of urinary retention at hospital discharge also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of urinary retention at hospital discharge will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for urinary retention at hospital discharge, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in urinary retention at hospital discharge is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no urinary retention at hospital discharge.

```{r, include = FALSE}

  formula = urinary_retention_hospital_discharge_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_,

We consider umbilical vein pH < 7.10.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 45* displays the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 45: Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHVENE_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHVENE_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich1_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich1_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Vein pH Less Than 7.10 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 46* displays the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 46: Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHVENE_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHVENE_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich1_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich1_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Vein pH Less Than 7.10 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 very strange, but this is because there are no subjects with umbilical vein pH < 7.10 in the upper three BMI categories. Nevertheless, the analyses of umbilical vein pH < 7.10 will be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical vein pH < 7.10 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical vein pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10 based on the multiple imputed FA set
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1 <- with(
  data = NSPHVENE_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHVENE_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHVENE_dich1_model1)
summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSPHVENE_dich1_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich1_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical vein pH < 7.10 is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10 based on the FA set
NSPHVENE_dich1_model3 <- glm(
  formula = NSPHVENE_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSPHVENE_dich1_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSPHVENE_dich1_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSPHVENE_dich1_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich1_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSPHVENE_dich1_model3, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in umbilical vein pH < 7.10 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical vein pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.10 based on the multiple imputed PP set
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4 <- with(
  data = NSPHVENE_multiple_imputation_PP_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHVENE_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHVENE_dich1_model4)
summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}

  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich1_model4_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider umbilical vein pH < 7.20.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 47* displays the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 47: Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHVENE_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHVENE_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich2_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich2_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Vein pH Less Than 7.20 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 48* displays the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 48: Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHVENE_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHVENE_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich2_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHVENE_dich2_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Vein pH Less Than 7.20 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 very strange, but this is because there are no subjects with umbilical vein pH < 7.20 in the upper three BMI categories. Nevertheless, the analyses of umbilical vein pH < 7.20 will be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.20, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. #### Sensitivity Analyses

##### Crude Analysis

tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHVENE_dich2_model2_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich2_model2_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich2_model2_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich2_model2_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.20, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical vein pH < 7.20 is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical vein pH < 7.20 based on the FA set
NSPHVENE_dich2_model3 <- glm(
  formula = NSPHVENE_dich2 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSPHVENE_dich2_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSPHVENE_dich2_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model

tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSPHVENE_dich2_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSPHVENE_dich2_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSPHVENE_dich2_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSPHVENE_dich2_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHVENE_dich2_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider umbilical artery pH < 7.00.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 49* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 49: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich1_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich1_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.00 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 50* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 50: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich1_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich1, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich1_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich1_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.00 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 very strange, but this is because there are no subjects with umbilical artery pH < 7.00 in the upper three BMI categories. Nevertheless, the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.00 will be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.00, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.00 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical artery pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.00 based on the multiple imputed FA set
NSPHART_dich1_model1 <- with(
  data = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHART_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHART_dich1_model1_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHART_dich1_model1)
summary(NSPHART_dich1_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHART_dich1_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich1_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHART_dich1_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHART_dich1_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich1_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSPHART_dich1_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich1_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHART_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHART_dich1_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich1_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.00, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.00 is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.00 based on the FA set
NSPHART_dich1_model3 <- glm(
  formula = NSPHART_dich1 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSPHART_dich1_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSPHART_dich1_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}

tmp1 <- summary(NSPHART_dich1_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSPHART_dich1_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSPHART_dich1_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSPHART_dich1_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSPHART_dich1_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich1_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich1_model3_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHART_dich1_model3_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHART_dich1_model3_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich1_model3_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

### Umbilical Artery pH < 7.10

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- NS %>% select(SubjectId, NSPHART_dich2, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
NSPHART_dich2_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation = NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
NSPHART_dich2_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation = NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
NSPHART_dich2_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation = NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set, 
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  ) %>% 
  select(-c(NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_ITT_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_FA_set, NSPHART_dich2_mean_imputation_PP_set))
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
# NOTE: This is based on the multiple imputation of umbilical artery pH.
NSPHART_multiple_imputation_ITT_set <- as.mids(long = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_ITT_set_complete)
NSPHART_multiple_imputation_FA_set <- as.mids(long = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_FA_set_complete)
NSPHART_multiple_imputation_PP_set <- as.mids(long = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_PP_set_complete)
```

We consider umbilical artery pH < 7.10.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 51* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 51: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich2_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich2_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.10 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 52* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 52: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich2_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich2, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich2_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich2_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.10 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 very strange, but this is because there are no subjects with umbilical artery pH < 7.10 in the upper three BMI categories. Nevertheless, the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.10 will be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.10, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.10 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical artery pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.10 based on the multiple imputed FA set
NSPHART_dich2_model1 <- with(
  data = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHART_dich2 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHART_dich2_model1_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHART_dich2_model1)
summary(NSPHART_dich2_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHART_dich2_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich2_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich2_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSPHART_dich2_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}

  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Umbilical artery pH < 7.10", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Dichotomous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Main analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4),

    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Multiple imputation of umbilical artery before dichotomization", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = mean(x = sapply(X = NSPHART_dich2_model1$analyses, FUN = nobs)), times = 4),

    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4),

    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(NSPHART_dich2_model1_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA),

  )

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.10, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.10 is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.10 based on the FA set

  formula = NSPHART_dich2 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSPHART_dich2_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)

tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSPHART_dich2_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSPHART_dich2_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSPHART_dich2_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich2_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
