We consider umbilical artery pH < 7.20.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 53* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 53: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich3_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich3_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich3_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.20 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 54* displays the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 54: Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSPHART_dich3_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSPHART_dich3, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich3_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSPHART_dich3_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Umbilical Artery pH Less Than 7.20 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 very strange, but this is because there are no subjects with umbilical artery pH < 7.20 in the upper three BMI categories. Nevertheless, the analyses of umbilical artery pH < 7.20 will be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.20 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical artery pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20 based on the multiple imputed FA set
NSPHART_dich3_model1 <- with(
  data = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_FA_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHART_dich3 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHART_dich3_model1_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHART_dich3_model1)
summary(NSPHART_dich3_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHART_dich3_model1_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)[2:4,]
tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich3_model1_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHART_dich3_model1_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHART_dich3_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich3_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model

  model = NSPHART_dich3_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich3_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSPHART_dich3_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSPHART_dich3_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich3_model1_results_margins
```
```{r, include = TRUE}
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.20 is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20 based on the FA set
NSPHART_dich3_model3 <- glm(
  formula = NSPHART_dich3 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSPHART_dich3_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSPHART_dich3_model3)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSPHART_dich3_model3)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSPHART_dich3_model3, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSPHART_dich3_model3_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSPHART_dich3_model3_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSPHART_dich3_model3_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich3_model3_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
)

tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100

NSPHART_dich3_model3_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in umbilical artery pH < 7.20 is handled implicitly by dichotomizing umbilical artery pH with imputed values after using multiple imputation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for umbilical artery pH < 7.20 based on the multiple imputed PP set
NSPHART_dich3_model4 <- with(
  data = NSPHART_multiple_imputation_PP_set, 
  expr = glm(
    formula = NSPHART_dich3 ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
    family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
    na.action = na.omit
  )
)
NSPHART_dich3_model4_pooled <- pool(object = NSPHART_dich3_model4)
summary(NSPHART_dich3_model4_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model

tmp2 <- substr(x = as.character(tmp1$term), start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = as.character(tmp1$term), type = "chars"))
tmp3 <- exp(x = tmp1$estimate)
tmp4 <- exp(x = tmp1$`2.5 %`)
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1$`97.5 %`)
tmp6 <- tmp1$p.value
NSPHART_dich3_model4_results <- cbind(tmp3, tmp4, tmp5, tmp6)
rownames(NSPHART_dich3_model4_results) <- tmp2
colnames(NSPHART_dich3_model4_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSPHART_dich3_model4_results
```
```{r, include = TRUE}
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### 5-Minute Apgar Score < 7

```{r, include = FALSE}

NSAPSC5_dich_PP_set <- PP_set %>%
```

We consider 5-minute Apgar score < 7.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 55* displays the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 55: Log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSAPSC5_dich_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSAPSC5_dich, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC5_dich_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC5_dich_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of 5-Minute Apgar Score Less Than 7 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 56* displays the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 56: Log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSAPSC5_dich_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSAPSC5_dich, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC5_dich_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC5_dich_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of 5-Minute Apgar Score Less Than 7 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for 5-minute Apgar score < 7, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in 5-minute Apgar score < 7 is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being 5-minute Apgar score >= 7.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for 5-minute Apgar score < 7 based on the FA set

  formula = NSAPSC5_dich_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSAPSC5_dich_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSAPSC5_dich_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

rownames(NSAPSC5_dich_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSAPSC5_dich_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSAPSC5_dich_model1_results
```
```{r, include = TRUE}
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Worst-Case (Single) Imputation

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for 5-minute Apgar score < 7, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in 5-minute Apgar score < 7 is handled using worst-case (single) imputation, with the worst-case scenario being Apgar score < 7.

```{r, include = FALSE}

  formula = NSAPSC5_dich_worst_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
```
```{r, include = FALSE}
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSAPSC5_dich_FA_set, 
```
```{r, include = FALSE}
  na.action = na.omit
```

### 10-Minute Apgar Score < 7

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- NS %>% select(SubjectId, NSAPSC10_dich, NSAPSC10_dich_best_case, NSAPSC10_dich_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
NSAPSC10_dich_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
NSAPSC10_dich_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
NSAPSC10_dich_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider 10-minute Apgar score < 7.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 57* displays the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 57: Log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSAPSC10_dich_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSAPSC10_dich, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC10_dich_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC10_dich_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of 10-Minute Apgar Score Less Than 7 as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 looks fairly linear, and the analyses of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 58* displays the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 58: Log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSAPSC10_dich_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSAPSC10_dich, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC10_dich_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSAPSC10_dich_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of 10-Minute Apgar Score Less Than 7 as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of 10-minute Apgar score < 7 will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for 10-minute Apgar score < 7, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in 10-minute Apgar score < 7 is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being 10-minute Apgar score >= 7.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for 10-minute Apgar score < 7 based on the FA set
NSAPSC10_dich_model1 <- glm(
  formula = NSAPSC10_dich_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSAPSC10_dich_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSAPSC10_dich_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSAPSC10_dich_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSAPSC10_dich_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSAPSC10_dich_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Creating a tibble for the results from the statistical analysis of the secondary endpoints
results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "10-minute Apgar score < 7", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Dichotomous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Main analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "None", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Binary logistic regression", times = 4), 
    `Adjustment` = rep(x = "Age (continuous), BMI (continuous), main indication for induction (categorical), and site (categorical)", times = 4), 
    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Best-case (single) imputation", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = nobs(object = NSAPSC10_dich_model1), times = 4), 
    `Allocated treatment` = c(rownames(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results), "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4), 
    `Point estiamte` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results[, "Odds ratio"], 1), 
    `Lower 95% confidence limit` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Upper 95% confidence limit` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `P value` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Marginal effect measure` = rep(x = "Risk difference", times = 4), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins[, "Risk difference"], 0), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(NSAPSC10_dich_model1_results_margins[, "P value"], NA), 
```
```{r, include = FALSE}
    `Comments` = rep(x = "", times = 4)
```
```{r, include = FALSE}
  )
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSAPSC10_dich_model5, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))

tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

rownames(NSAPSC10_dich_model5_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSAPSC10_dich_model5_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSAPSC10_dich_model5_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
NSAPSC10_dich_model5_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

### Admission to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Defining the data frames to be used in the analyses
tmp1 <- NS %>% select(SubjectId, NSNICUYNCD, NSNICUYNCD_best_case, NSNICUYNCD_worst_case)
tmp2 <- DM %>% select(SubjectId, DMAGE, DMAGE_cat_factor)
tmp3 <- PE %>% select(SubjectId, PEBMI, PEBMI_cat_factor)
tmp4 <- IN %>% select(SubjectId, ININD)
NSNICUYNCD_ITT_set <- ITT_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
NSNICUYNCD_FA_set <- FA_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
NSNICUYNCD_PP_set <- PP_set %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp1, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp2, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp3, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  left_join(y = tmp4, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  rename(
    Site_ = SiteName, 
    Age = DMAGE, 
    Age_categorized_ = DMAGE_cat_factor, 
    BMI = PEBMI, 
    BMI_categorized_ = PEBMI_cat_factor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    Treatment_ = relevel(x = factor(x = Treatment_allocated_str), ref = "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo"), 
    Main_indication_for_induction_ = relevel(x = factor(x = ININD), ref = "Postdates (as defined locally; latest 42+0 weeks)"), 
    .after = Treatment_allocated_num
  )
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

We consider admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.

#### Assumption Checks

First, we check the assumption of linear effect of age on the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit and the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age. *Figure 59* displays the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit as a function of age based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 59: Log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit as a function of age."}
# Plotting the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit against the midpoint of age within equal-ranged categories of age based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSNICUYNCD_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = Age, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSNICUYNCD, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSNICUYNCD_age <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit vs. age") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSNICUYNCD_age
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Admission to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit as a Function of Age.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of age on the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit looks fairly linear, and the analyses of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit will therefore be adjusted for age as a continuous variable.

Then, we check the assumption of linear effect of BMI on the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit. We aggregate the FA set by calculating the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit and the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI. *Figure 60* displays the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit as a function of BMI based on the aggregated data.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Figure 60: Log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit as a function of BMI. Abbreviations: BMI -- body mass index."}
# Plotting the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit against the midpoint of BMI within equal-ranged categories of BMI based on the aggregated FA set
# NOTE: We add a 95% confidence interval around the linear smoothed line.
tmp <- NSNICUYNCD_FA_set %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = cut_interval(x = BMI, n = 5)) %>% 
  group_by(tmp1) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmp2 = mean(NSNICUYNCD, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = log(x = tmp2 / (1 - tmp2), base = exp(1)), 
    tmp4 = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(tmp6 = mean(x = c(tmp4, tmp5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()
plot_log_odds_NSNICUYNCD_BMI <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(x = tmp6, y = tmp3)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, level = 0.95, color = "blue") + 
  labs(x = "BMI (kg/m^2)", y = "Log odds", title = "Log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit vs. BMI") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
plot_log_odds_NSNICUYNCD_BMI
ggsave(filename = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Log Odds of Admission to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit as a Function of BMI.png"), plot = last_plot(), device = "png", width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

The effect of BMI on the log odds of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit also looks fairly linear, and the analyses of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit will therefore be adjusted for BMI as a continuous variable.

#### Main Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in admission to the neonatal intensive care unit is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit based on the FA set
NSNICUYNCD_model1 <- glm(
  formula = NSNICUYNCD_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSNICUYNCD_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSNICUYNCD_model1)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSNICUYNCD_model1)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSNICUYNCD_model1, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSNICUYNCD_model1_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model1_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSNICUYNCD_model1_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSNICUYNCD_model1_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSNICUYNCD_model1, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSNICUYNCD_model1_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model1_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSNICUYNCD_model1_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSNICUYNCD_model1_results_margins
```
```{r, include = TRUE}
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

##### Complete-Case Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the FA set. Missingness in admission to the neonatal intensive care unit is handled using complete-case analysis (i.e., ignoring observations with any missing values).

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit based on the FA set
NSNICUYNCD_model4 <- glm(
  formula = NSNICUYNCD ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSNICUYNCD_FA_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSNICUYNCD_model4)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- summary(NSNICUYNCD_model4)$coefficients[2:4,]
tmp2 <- rownames(tmp1)
tmp3 <- exp(x = confint(object = NSNICUYNCD_model4, parm = tmp2, level = 0.95))
tmp4 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = nchar(x = "Treatment_", type = "chars") + 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars"))
tmp5 <- exp(x = tmp1[, "Estimate"])
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSNICUYNCD_model4_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSNICUYNCD_model4_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

```{r, include = TRUE}
# Calculating the marginal risk differences with 95% confidence intervals based on the fitted regression model
tmp1 <- avg_comparisons(
  model = NSNICUYNCD_model4, 
  variables = "Treatment_", 
  type = "response", 
  conf_level = 0.95, 
  comparison = "difference"
)
tmp2 <- tmp1$contrast
tmp3 <- substr(x = tmp2, start = 1, stop = nchar(x = tmp2, type = "chars") - nchar(x = " - Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo", type = "chars"))
tmp4 <- tmp1$estimate * 100
tmp5 <- tmp1$conf.low * 100
tmp6 <- tmp1$conf.high * 100
tmp7 <- tmp1$p.value
NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins <- cbind(tmp4, tmp5, tmp6, tmp7)
rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins) <- tmp3
colnames(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins) <- c("Risk difference", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Creating a tibble for the results from the statistical analysis of the secondary endpoints
results_secondary <- results_secondary %>% 
  add_row(
    `Endpoint` = rep(x = "Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit", times = 4), 
    `Type of endpoint` = rep(x = "Dichotomous", times = 4), 
    `Type of analysis` = rep(x = "Sensitivity analysis", times = 4), 
    `Analysis set` = rep(x = "FA set", times = 4), 
    `Restriction of analysis set` = rep(x = "None", times = 4), 
    `Analysis method` = rep(x = "Binary logistic regression", times = 4), 
    `Adjustment` = rep(x = "Age (continuous), BMI (continuous), main indication for induction (categorical), and site (categorical)", times = 4), 
    `Handling of missing data` = rep(x = "Complete-case analysis", times = 4), 
    `Sample size` = rep(x = nobs(object = NSNICUYNCD_model4), times = 4), 
    `Allocated treatment` = c(rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results), "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
    `Effect measure` = rep(x = "Odds ratio", times = 4), 
    `Point estiamte` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results[, "Odds ratio"], 1), 
    `Lower 95% confidence limit` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Upper 95% confidence limit` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `P value` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results[, "P value"], NA), 
    `Marginal effect measure` = rep(x = "Risk difference", times = 4), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins[, "Risk difference"], 0), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins[, "Lower 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins[, "Upper 95% confidence limit"], NA), 
    `Marginal P value` = c(NSNICUYNCD_model4_results_margins[, "P value"], NA),

  )
```

##### PP Analysis

We fit an adjusted binary logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, including allocated treatment (4-level categorical variable), age (continuous variable), BMI (continuous variable), main indication for induction (15-level categorical variable), and site (11-level categorical variable) with fixed effects. The analysis is based on the PP set. Missingness in admission to the neonatal intensive care unit is handled using best-case (single) imputation, with the best-case scenario being no admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Fitting an adjusted logistic regression model for admission to the neonatal intensive care unit based on the PP set
NSNICUYNCD_model5 <- glm(
  formula = NSNICUYNCD_best_case ~ Treatment_ + Age + BMI + Main_indication_for_induction_ + Site_, 
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
  data = NSNICUYNCD_PP_set, 
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(NSNICUYNCD_model5)
```

```{r, include = TRUE}
tmp6 <- tmp3[, 1]
tmp7 <- tmp3[, 2]
tmp8 <- tmp1[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
NSNICUYNCD_model5_results <- cbind(tmp5, tmp6, tmp7, tmp8)
rownames(NSNICUYNCD_model5_results) <- tmp4
colnames(NSNICUYNCD_model5_results) <- c("Odds ratio", "Lower 95% confidence limit", "Upper 95% confidence limit", "P value")
NSNICUYNCD_model5_results
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

Based on the fitted regression model, we calculate the marginal risk differences using the delta method.

## Summary of Endpoints Related to Mode of Delivery

*Figure X* displays the results of the main analyses of spontaneous vaginal delivery.

```{r, include = TRUE, fig.cap = "Figure X: Results of the main analysis of spontaneous vaginal delivery."}
# Creating a plot of the results of the main analysis of spontaneous vaginal delivery
tmp <- results_primary %>% 
  filter(Endpoint == "Spontaneous vaginal delivery" & `Type of analysis` == "Main analysis") %>% 
  select(Endpoint, `Sample size`, `Allocated treatment`, `Marginal effect measure`, `Marginal point estimate`, `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, `Marginal P value`) %>% 
  mutate(
    `Allocated treatment` = factor(
      x = `Allocated treatment`, 
      levels = c("Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
      labels = c("Bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide", "Bicarbonate", "Hyoscine butylbromide", "Double placebo (ref.)")
    ), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = round(x = `Marginal point estimate`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = round(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = round(x = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal P value` = round(x = `Marginal P value`, digits = 3), 
    tmp1 = case_when(
      `Allocated treatment` == "Double placebo (ref.)"                  ~ 1, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Hyoscine butylbromide"                  ~ 2, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Bicarbonate"                            ~ 3, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide" ~ 4, 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp2 = min(`Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = max(`Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp4 = max(abs(x = tmp2), abs(x = tmp3), na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp5 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal point estimate`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal point estimate`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp6 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp7 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp8 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal P value`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal P value`, nsmall = 3), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp9 = case_when(
      !is.na(tmp5) & !is.na(tmp6) & !is.na(tmp7) & !is.na(tmp8) ~ paste(tmp5, " (95% CI ", tmp6, " to ", tmp7, "; P=", tmp8, ")", sep = ""), 
      .default = NULL
    )
  )
plot_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery <- ggplot(data = tmp, mapping = aes(color = `Allocated treatment`)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + 
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, xend = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, y = tmp1, yend = tmp1)) + 
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = -tmp4, xend = tmp4, y = 1, yend = 1), color = "transparent") + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal point estimate`, y = tmp1)) + 
  geom_text(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal point estimate`, y = tmp1, label = tmp9), color = "black", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, nudge_y = -0.25, size = 2.5) + 
  labs(
    title = "Spontaneous vaginal birth vs operative delivery", 
    tag = "A", 
    x = "Average marginal effect", 
    y = NULL
  ) + 
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      title = "Treatment arm", 
      direction = "vertical", 
      nrow = 1, 
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  ) + 
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12), 
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), 
    legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    legend.position = "none"
  )
plot_spontaneous_vaginal_delivery
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Saving the plot as a PDF file
ggsave(
  filename = "Results of the Main Analysis of Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "pdf", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)

# Saving the plot as a PNG file
ggsave(
  filename = "Results of the Main Analysis of Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery.png", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "png", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Summary of Neonatal Secondary Endpoints

*Figure X* displays the results of the respective main analyses of neonatal secondary endpoints.

```{r, include = TRUE, fig.cap = "Figure X: Results of the respective main analyses of neonatal secondary endpoints."}
# Creating a plot of the results of the respective main analyses of neonatal secondary endpoints
tmp1 <- c("Umbilical artery pH < 7.00", "Umbilical artery pH < 7.10", "Umbilical artery pH < 7.20", "Umbilical vein pH < 7.10", "Umbilical vein pH < 7.20", "5-minute Apgar score < 7", "10-minute Apgar score < 7", "Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit")
tmp2 <- results_secondary %>% 
  filter(Endpoint %in% get(x = "tmp1", envir = globalenv()) & `Type of analysis` == "Main analysis") %>% 
  select(Endpoint, `Sample size`, `Allocated treatment`, `Marginal effect measure`, `Marginal point estimate`, `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, `Marginal P value`) %>% 
  mutate(
    Endpoint = factor(
      x = Endpoint, 
      levels = get(x = "tmp1", envir = globalenv())
    ), 
    `Allocated treatment` = factor(
      x = `Allocated treatment`, 
      levels = c("Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral bicarbonate & intravenous placebo", "Peroral placebo & intravenous hyoscine butylbromide", "Peroral placebo & intravenous placebo (ref.)"), 
      labels = c("Bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide", "Bicarbonate", "Hyoscine butylbromide", "Double placebo (ref.)")
    ), 
    `Marginal point estimate` = round(x = `Marginal point estimate`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit` = round(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit` = round(x = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, digits = 2), 
    `Marginal P value` = round(x = `Marginal P value`, digits = 3), 
    tmp1 = case_when(
      `Allocated treatment` == "Double placebo (ref.)"                  ~ 1, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Hyoscine butylbromide"                  ~ 2, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Bicarbonate"                            ~ 3, 
      `Allocated treatment` == "Bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide" ~ 4, 
      .default = NULL
    )
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Endpoint) %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp2 = min(`Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp3 = max(`Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, na.rm = TRUE), 
    tmp4 = max(abs(x = tmp2), abs(x = tmp3), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp5 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal point estimate`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal point estimate`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp6 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp7 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, nsmall = 2), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp8 = case_when(
      !is.na(`Marginal P value`) ~ trimws(x = format(x = `Marginal P value`, nsmall = 3), which = "both"), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp9 = case_when(
      !is.na(tmp5) & !is.na(tmp6) & !is.na(tmp7) & !is.na(tmp8) ~ paste(tmp5, " (95% CI ", tmp6, " to ", tmp7, ")", sep = ""), 
      .default = NULL
    )
  )
plot_neonatal_secondary_endpoints <- ggplot(data = tmp2, mapping = aes(color = `Allocated treatment`)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + 
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal lower 95% confidence limit`, xend = `Marginal upper 95% confidence limit`, y = tmp1, yend = tmp1)) + 
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = -tmp4, xend = tmp4, y = 1, yend = 1), color = "transparent") + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal point estimate`, y = tmp1)) + 
  geom_text(mapping = aes(x = `Marginal point estimate`, y = tmp1, label = tmp9), color = "black", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, nudge_y = -0.4, size = 2.5) + 
  facet_wrap(
    facets = vars(Endpoint), 
    nrow = 4, 
    scales = "free_x", 
    dir = "h"
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Neonatal endpoints", 
    x = "Average marginal effect", 
    y = NULL
  ) + 
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      title = "Treatment arm", 
      direction = "vertical", 
      nrow = 1, 
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  ) + 
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12), 
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), 
    legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
plot_neonatal_secondary_endpoints
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Saving the plot as a PDF file
ggsave(
  filename = "Results of the Main Analysis of Neonatal Secondary Endpoints.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "pdf", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)

# Saving the plot as a PNG file
ggsave(
  filename = "Results of the Main Analysis of Neonatal Secondary Endpoints.png", 
  plot = last_plot(), 
  device = "png", 
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files"), 
  width = 12, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Safety Analyses

Safety analyses are based on adverse events and vital signs.

## Adverse Events

*Table X* displays the respective numbers of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) per subject among subjects in the safety set (*n* = `r dim(safety_set)[1]`), overall and by treatment group. The numbers per subject are presented with absolute and relative frequencies (i.e., numbers and percentages). The total numbers across subjects are presented within square brackets.

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
# Creating a table of summary statistics
tmp1 <- tribble(
  ~ desc, ~ var, ~ fun, ~ par, 
  "Any AE",                              "",     "calculate_no_summary_statistics",           list(), 
  "- No",                                "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2", list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- Yes",                               "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "Number of AEs",                       "",     "calculate_no_summary_statistics",           list(), 
  "- 0",                                 "tmp5", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2", list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- 1",                                 "tmp5", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- 2",                                 "tmp5", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "2"), 
  paste("- ", "\U2265", " 3", sep = ""), "tmp5", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "3")
)
tmp2 <- AE %>% 
  select(SubjectId) %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = 1) %>% 
  left_join(x = safety_set, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  mutate(tmp2 = if_else(condition = is.na(tmp1), true = 0, false = tmp1, missing = NULL)) %>% 
  group_by(SubjectId) %>% 
  mutate(tmp3 = sum(tmp2, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp4 = case_when(
      tmp2 == 0 & tmp3 == 0 ~ 0, 
      tmp2 == 1             ~ if_else(tmp3 >= 1, true = 1, false = tmp3, missing = NULL), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp5 = case_when(
      tmp2 == 0 & tmp3 == 0 ~ 0, 
      tmp2 == 1             ~ if_else(tmp3 >= 3, true = 3, false = tmp3, missing = NULL), 
      .default = NULL
    )
  )
tmp3 <- tmp2 %>% 
  bind_rows(tmp2 %>% mutate(Treatment_allocated_str = "Overall"))
table_AE_number <- create_table_summary_statistics(table = tmp1, data = tmp3, group = "Treatment_allocated_str")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Creating a table of summary statistics
tmp1 <- tribble(
  ~ desc, ~ var, ~ fun, ~ par, 
  "Any SAE",                             "",     "calculate_no_summary_statistics",           list(), 
  "- No",                                "tmp3", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2", list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- Yes",                               "tmp3", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "Number of SAEs",                      "",     "calculate_no_summary_statistics",           list(), 
  "- 0",                                 "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical2", list(digits = 1, level = "0"), 
  "- 1",                                 "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "1"), 
  "- 2",                                 "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "2"), 
  paste("- ", "\U2265", " 3", sep = ""), "tmp4", "calculate_summary_statistics_categorical1", list(digits = 1, level = "3")
)
tmp2 <- AE %>% 
  select(SubjectId, AESERCD) %>% 
  left_join(x = safety_set, by = "SubjectId") %>% 
  mutate(tmp1 = if_else(condition = is.na(AESERCD), true = 0, false = AESERCD, missing = NULL)) %>% 
  group_by(SubjectId) %>% 
  mutate(tmp2 = sum(tmp1, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    tmp3 = case_when(
      tmp1 == 0 & tmp2 == 0 ~ 0, 
      tmp1 == 1             ~ if_else(tmp2 >= 1, true = 1, false = tmp2, missing = NULL), 
      .default = NULL
    ), 
    tmp4 = case_when(
      tmp1 == 0 & tmp2 == 0 ~ 0, 
      tmp1 == 1             ~ if_else(tmp2 >= 3, true = 3, false = tmp2, missing = NULL), 
      .default = NULL
    )
  )
tmp3 <- tmp2 %>% 
  bind_rows(tmp2 %>% mutate(Treatment_allocated_str = "Overall"))
table_SAE_number <- create_table_summary_statistics(table = tmp1, data = tmp3, group = "Treatment_allocated_str")
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Binding the data frames by row
table_AE_SAE_number <- bind_rows(table_AE_number, table_SAE_number)
write_xlsx(x = table_AE_SAE_number, path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Number of Adverse Events and Serious Adverse Events.xlsx"), col_names = TRUE, format_headers = TRUE)

# Creating a table in HTML
tmp1 <- dim(table_AE_SAE_number)[2]
tmp2 <- 0
tmp3 <- (1:dim(table_AE_SAE_number)[1])[which(substr(x = table_AE_SAE_number$Characteristic, start = 1, stop = 1) != "-")]
knitr::kable(x = table_AE_SAE_number, format = "html", align = c("l", rep(x = "c", times = tmp1 - 1)), caption = paste("Table X: Number of adverse events and serious adverse events in the safety set (", dim(safety_set)[1], " subjects), overall and by treatment group. Abbreviations: AE -- adverse event; SAE -- serious adverse event.", sep = "")) %>% kable_classic(full_width = TRUE, html_font = "Computer Modern") %>% row_spec(row = tmp2, bold = TRUE) %>% row_spec(row = tmp3, italic = TRUE)
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
table_SAE_soc_pt2B <- create_table_summary_statistics_MedDRA2(data = tmp2, group = "Treatment_allocated_str", filter = "AESERCD", digits = 1)
write_xlsx(x = table_SAE_soc_pt2B, path = file.path(getwd(), "Output Files", "Serious Adverse Events per System Organ Class and Preferred Term in the Safety Set - Version 2B.xlsx"), col_names = TRUE, format_headers = TRUE)
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))

# Creating a table in HTML
tmp1 <- 2
tmp2 <- dim(table_SAE_soc_pt2B)[2] - tmp1
tmp3 <- 0
knitr::kable(x = table_SAE_soc_pt2B, format = "html", align = c(rep(x = "l", times = tmp1), rep(x = "c", times = tmp2)), caption = paste("Table X: Serious adverse evens per system organ class and preferred term in the safety set restricted to subjects with at least one serious adverse event (", AE %>% filter(AESERCD == 1) %>% semi_join(y = safety_set, by = "SubjectId") %>% select(SubjectId) %>% deframe() %>% unique() %>% length(), " subjects), overall and by treatment group.", sep = "")) %>% kable_classic(full_width = TRUE, html_font = "Computer Modern") %>% row_spec(row = tmp3, bold = TRUE)
rm(list = ls(pattern = "^tmp"))
```

# Saving {.hidden .unlisted .unnumbered}

Finally, we save all relevant objects.
